Something is on every night on Koh Samui: Muay Thai fights in Chaweng six nights a week (none on Thursdays), the Fisherman's Village Walking Street every Friday from about 17:00, Chaweng Walking Street Thursday to Saturday and free beach fire shows on Chaweng from 20:00. The next big night is Tuesday 24 November 2026, when Loy Krathong and the Full Moon Party fall on the same date; then come the Christmas Eve Full Moon Party (24 December) and New Year's Eve (31 December). Our shared Full Moon speedboat from Samui costs 1,400 THB return with hotel pickup from most areas.

What's on in Koh Samui: live listings

The list below updates itself from our events calendar and shows the next 45 days. Filter by today, tomorrow, this weekend or by type (party, market, Muay Thai, festival, community). Past events drop off automatically. We re-check recurring listings every Monday and one-off dates as soon as an organiser publishes or changes them.

Good to know: November is Samui's wettest month (about 445 mm of rain on 16 days on average). Outdoor markets and beach fire shows run "weather permitting" in November and December, and a heavy shower can close a walking street early. Check the forecast on Windy before you set out.

Every week on Koh Samui: the weekday calendar

Samui's regular nightlife runs on a fixed weekly rhythm. The two Muay Thai stadiums split the week between them, the big markets have fixed nights, and the beach bars in Chaweng, Lamai and Fisherman's Village run fire shows most evenings. Use this table to plan the week; the sections below give times, prices and the catches.

Markets and walking streets

The Fisherman's Village Walking Street in Bophut is the one market worth planning a night around: the beach road from The Wharf to the far end of the village closes to traffic on Friday afternoons (about 16:30) and fills with street food, crafts and bars until about 23:00. Pad thai costs about 60–80 THB, mango sticky rice 50–80 THB and grilled prawns 80–120 THB; a full market dinner runs 300–500 THB per person. Arrive before 18:00 or you will queue to park. Monday and Wednesday are smaller, more local nights at The Wharf end. Chaweng Walking Street, opposite Central Samui by Chaweng Lake, runs Thursday to Saturday. The old Maenam Thursday and Lamai Sunday walking streets have been reported closed since the pandemic, and we don't list them until we confirm them on the ground. Full details are in our Koh Samui markets guide and the walking streets guide.

Muay Thai fight nights

Two stadiums in Chaweng share the week. Samui International Muay Thai Stadium fights on Tuesday, Friday and Sunday: doors open at 20:00 and the first bout starts at 21:30, finishing around midnight. Tickets are 1,500 THB (stadium), 2,000 THB (ringside), 2,500 THB (VIP) and 3,000 THB (VIP premium); children aged 6–10 pay half price and under-6s enter free. Phetchbuncha Stadium (Chaweng–Choeng Mon road, Soi 13 Chaweng Yai) fights on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday from 21:00, at 1,500 THB, 2,000 THB ringside and 2,500 THB VIP. There are no fights on Thursdays. The old Chaweng Stadium is reported closed and we found no current schedule for Lamai. Buy at the box office or a trusted desk, never from street touts. Seat advice and what to expect on the night are in our Muay Thai fight nights guide.

Ladyboy cabaret shows

Samui has two ladyboy cabarets on Chaweng Beach Road. Divas Cabaret runs three shows a night, at 20:30, 21:30 and 22:30, each about 45 minutes, with a drink minimum instead of a ticket; arrive early for the 21:30 show in peak season. Paris Follies Cabaret sits between Soi Bar Solo and Soi Green Mango (look for the Eiffel Tower sign). Its show lasts about 50 minutes and ticket packages that include a drink are sold. Shows run every night. Entry has traditionally been free if you buy a drink of about 350 THB or more [check]. The usual show times are about 20:30, 21:30 and 23:00 [check]. Starz Cabaret, the other famous Chaweng show, closed permanently in 2021, so ignore any listing that still sends you there. Tip performers only if you take a photo with them, and agree the amount first.

Fire shows and beach-club nights

Fire shows are free and nightly. ARKbar Beach Club on central Chaweng Beach runs fire dancers and DJs from 20:00 to 24:00; Elephant Beach Club further along the sand also has nightly fire shows. In Bophut, Coco Tam's beanbag bar runs fire shows at about 19:15 and 21:00 (some seating has a minimum spend). Lamai's Teddy Weed beach bar has fire shows and parties until about 02:00, and Cape Away in Maenam has fire performers at its Sunday party. Stand well back from the performers on the sand and keep children close. Our beach clubs guide and Koh Samui nightlife guide cover the venues in depth.

Every month: Full Moon and Half Moon parties from Samui

The Full Moon Party is not on Samui: it is on Haad Rin Nok (Sunrise Beach) on Koh Phangan, about 20–30 minutes by speedboat from Samui's north coast. It runs from the evening (the beach fills from about 21:00) until after sunrise, entry is about 200 THB at the gate, and the date moves a day or two whenever the full moon falls on a Buddhist holy day (because alcohol sales stop). Four 2027 dates are moved this way, and many websites still list the raw lunar dates, so check here before you book flights.

Half Moon Festival, Jungle Experience and Waterfall Party

The Half Moon Festival in Ban Tai, Koh Phangan, runs twice a month as a two-part event: a Harmony Beach Club day party (15:00–24:00), then the Halfmoon Magic Forest jungle night (21:00 to sunrise). The remaining 2026 Magic Forest nights are Thursday 3 December and Thursday 17 December; 3 and 17 November are beach-club days only. The organiser has not yet published 2027 dates. Jungle Experience in Ban Tai is usually the night before the Full Moon Party (Mon 23 Nov, Wed 23 Dec and the Wed 30 Dec "Grand Finale" in 2026), from 22:00 to about 06:00, minimum age 20 with ID. The Waterfall Party runs several nights a month, not tied to the moon (11, 22 and 26 November and 9, 22, 26 and 29 December 2026), from 21:00 until about 02:00–03:00. For the Phangan side of every party, see the Koh Phangan events listings on our sister site.

The big Koh Samui events, one by one

Full Moon Party from Samui

Fourteen lunar parties plus two New Year's Eve parties run between now and the end of 2027. From Samui the easiest way is a door-to-door speedboat: hotel pickup, a 20–30 minute crossing to Haad Rin and a hotel drop-off when you choose to come back. The ferry alternative, the Haad Rin Queen from Big Buddha pier, has only a few sailings a day, so you need your own way back at 04:00. Avoid driving a scooter to the pier and leaving it overnight. Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve boats sell out first; book them in November.

Loy Krathong: Tuesday 24 November 2026

Thais float a krathong (a small raft with a candle, incense and flowers) on water after dark to thank the water spirits and let go of bad luck. On Samui the classic spots are Chaweng Lake, the Big Buddha and the beaches; many hotels set up ponds. Buy a bread or banana-leaf krathong from a roadside stall rather than a foam one. Do not release sky lanterns: launching them near an airport is illegal in Thailand, Samui's airport sits between Chaweng and Bophut, and the island treats them as banned. In 2026 the Full Moon Party falls on the same night. Our Loy Krathong guide has the best spots.

Christmas and New Year's Eve

Christmas is not a Thai public holiday, but the resorts run dinners and brunches and Christmas Eve is a Full Moon Party night. On New Year's Eve the biggest fireworks are on Chaweng, then Fisherman's Village, Lamai, Maenam and Choeng Mon (the last two are the family choice). Central Samui has held a free countdown with concerts and midnight fireworks; the 2026 programme is not out yet. Resort galas (for example, 14,500 THB++ per person at one Bophut resort; "++" adds 10% service and 7% VAT) sell out by mid-December, and flights and ferries are full on 1–2 January.

Chinese New Year: Saturday 6 February 2027

Samui's Chinese families have Hainan roots. Maenam's Chinese temple and old Chinatown hold the family-friendly lion and dragon dances; Nathon's Hainan shrine holds the more traditional rites, which can include face-piercing that may not suit children; the 16 m bronze Guan Yu statue at Hua Thanon (open 09:00–17:00) also celebrates. February is the driest month (about 64 mm of rain), so it is the best week of the year for boat trips. The local programme is usually announced in January.

Songkran: 13–15 April 2027

Thailand's New Year is a three-day water fight. On Samui the street events usually start on 12 April, with official programmes in Bo Phut (Chaweng and Fisherman's Village), Maret (Lamai) and Ang Thong (Nathon). Chaweng Beach Road is the main battleground; beach clubs run pool parties and Central Samui has held a foam party from 12:00 to 24:00. Put your phone in a waterproof pouch, expect to be soaked by anyone on the street, and do not ride a scooter: roads are wet and drivers are drunk. Temples hold quieter merit-making in the mornings.

Samui Regatta: 22–29 May 2027

The 24th Samui Regatta brings a week of keelboat racing off Chaweng Beach, with beach parties and a closing gala; the 2026 edition was the 23rd. Watching from the beach is free. Late May is hot (around 33 °C) with mostly workable seas, which also makes it a good week for a private boat day. Details are on our Samui Regatta page, and private boats for spectating or a day out are on our private speedboat page.

Buffalo fighting

Buffalo fighting is a traditional southern Thai contest in which two bulls lock horns until one turns away, with heavy betting. On Samui it has been held at small village arenas around New Year and Songkran, announced only a few days ahead by loudspeaker trucks and banners. We found no confirmed 2025–2026 venues or dates, and because of welfare concerns we don't list, sell or give directions to fights. Our buffalo fighting explainer covers the history and the law.

Buddhist holy days and alcohol rules

Since 29 May 2026, shops in Thailand may sell alcohol from 11:00 to 24:00 (the old 14:00–17:00 afternoon ban has ended). Hotels and licensed entertainment venues are exempt from the hours and may open to about 02:00–04:00 depending on zone and licence. The legal drinking age is 20. On Buddhist holy days alcohol sales are banned nationwide, but since May 2025 hotels, licensed bars and entertainment venues in tourist areas may still serve; 7-Eleven, shops and unlicensed restaurants may not. There are no ban days in November or December 2026, and Loy Krathong, Songkran and Chinese New Year are not ban days.

Sports and community events

These recurring events are organised locally and announced only a few weeks ahead. The dates below are based on the 2025–2026 editions; treat them as provisional and confirm locally.

  • Samui Trail (ITRA-rated, 7, 15, 25 and 55 km): the 2026 edition is listed for Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November 2026; the 2025 edition was 8–9 November, with the 55 km starting at 23:00.
  • Samui Santa Run: a mid-December charity fun run (2025: Saturday 13 December).
  • Koh Samui Red Cross Fair: February, traditionally in Nathon, with a Thai traditional costume parade.
  • Samui Open Beach Volleyball: late March on the beach at Central Samui, Chaweng (2026: 26–29 March).
  • Central Samui Neon Run: a 5 km and 10 km night run along Chaweng Road in late May (2026: Saturday 30 May, about 3,000 runners).
  • Samui Half Marathon: June, with a kids' run the day before (2026: Sunday 21 June).

No current Samui triathlon or jazz festival is running, and the old TAT "Samui Festival" has not been held since 2019.

How to get to events and back

Most nightlife is in Chaweng, 15–20 minutes from Bophut and 20–25 minutes from Lamai by car. Getting there is easy; getting home after midnight is the part to plan.

On Friday the Fisherman's Village beach road closes at about 16:30 and scooters parked in the wrong place are towed (500 THB or more to release); use the paid car park at The Wharf. For the Full Moon Party, a door-to-door boat avoids the late-night ferry problem entirely. More on taxis, Grab and scooters is in our getting around Koh Samui guide.

Safety at night

Stay safe

The UK Foreign Office warns of assaults, including sexual assaults, drink spiking and unlicensed transport around the Full Moon Party and in nightlife areas. Watch your drink being made, keep it with you, and stay with your group. Never swim after drinking: Chaweng and Lamai have rip currents and red flags from October to December, and drownings have followed ignored red flags. Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal in Thailand (fines and detention, and extortion demands have been reported). Buying cannabis needs a prescription and smoking it in public can be fined up to 25,000 THB. Carry a copy of your passport, not the original. Common late-night scams (bar bills, touts, jet-ski "damage" claims) are in our scams guide.

Emergency numbers: Tourist Police 1155 (English), police 191, ambulance 1669, fire 199.

Where to stay for nightlife

Stay in central or north Chaweng if you want to walk home from the clubs and the Muay Thai. Fisherman's Village suits couples who want a good dinner and a quieter bar; Lamai has a smaller scene with an older crowd. Choeng Mon, Maenam and the west coast are quiet after dark. Our where to stay guide compares the areas.

The day after

After a Full Moon night, an afternoon on the water is the easiest recovery: the Pig Island Sunset Tour (1,550 THB adult, 1,350 THB child, dinner included) leaves in the early afternoon, so you can sleep in.

Party at night, the sea by day

Pair the nights with a day on the water. Pig Island and Koh Tan by speedboat (1,450 THB) runs every day of the year. The Ang Thong Marine Park speedboat tour (1,800 THB) runs from 16 December to 31 October; the park closes every year from 1 November to 15 December. For a group, a private speedboat goes where and when you want.
